title: Independent Source Reading
description: Meet a source you have not studied in this sequence. Orient yourself before making a claim: identify its voice, its work, and one bounded connection.

encounters.hebrew: וזכרת את כל הדרך אשר הוליכך ה׳ אלהיך
encounters.translation: Remember the whole way that the Lord your God led you.
encounters.context: A wilderness memory becomes a call to interpret present life through a remembered journey.

questions.prompt: What is the safest first observation?

choices.text: The line addresses a listener and commands remembering a shared journey.
The line supplies a detailed legal ruling.
The line is a later Talmudic objection.

questions.explanation: Begin with the speaker, addressee, and the verb before importing later meanings.

choices.text: It can be compared with prayerful memory, while keeping Torah narrative and liturgy distinct.
It proves every prayer text has the same function.
It should never be connected to later Jewish reading.

questions.explanation: A connection should preserve both continuity and difference.

encounters.context: A psalm uses imperative language to shape a communal posture of worship.

questions.prompt: What is this source primarily doing?

choices.text: Calling a community toward a posture of worship.
Measuring the boundary of a legal obligation.
Reporting a historical event without exhortation.

questions.explanation: Its imperative voice and worship setting matter before application.

questions.prompt: What is a bounded next move?

choices.text: Compare its posture with praise and thanks in the Amidah, without treating them as identical.
Use it as a personal ruling for every emotional state.
Ignore its language because it is poetic.

questions.explanation: Liturgical comparison notices function, genre, and setting.

encounters.translation: Do not separate yourself from the community.
encounters.context: A compact rabbinic maxim presents ethical formation in a memorable form.

questions.prompt: What kind of source move is most visible?

choices.text: An ethical maxim about communal belonging.
A verse whose grammar alone resolves a legal case.
A report from one historical archive.

questions.explanation: Name genre and function before making a broad claim.

questions.prompt: Which application keeps an appropriate boundary?

choices.text: Ask what forms of participation and responsibility this maxim might invite in a specific community.
Declare that it settles every disagreement with a community.
Treat it as unrelated to any lived practice.

questions.explanation: Ethical learning supports reflection, not automatic rulings.

encounters.translation: Everything is foreseen, yet permission is given.
encounters.context: A concise saying holds two claims in tension rather than dissolving the difficulty immediately.

questions.prompt: What makes this a conceptual source?

choices.text: It places two claims in tension and invites interpretation.
It merely labels a topic without making a claim.
It gives a geographic description.

questions.explanation: Conceptual reading begins by stating the claims accurately.

questions.prompt: What is the strongest connection to Deuteronomy 30?

choices.text: Both concern agency, but one commands choosing and the other frames a philosophical tension.
They are interchangeable statements with no difference.
Neither source has any bearing on agency.

questions.explanation: Good comparison names the shared question and the difference in what each source does.

encounters.hebrew: ודרשו את שלום העיר אשר הגליתי אתכם שמה
encounters.translation: Seek the welfare of the city to which I have exiled you.
encounters.context: A prophetic message addresses a displaced community in a particular imperial setting.

questions.prompt: Which question should guide an initial reading?

choices.text: Who is addressed, where are they, and what situation gives this command force?
Which current debate does it automatically decide?
How can its setting be ignored most quickly?

questions.explanation: Historical setting is evidence, not decorative background.

choices.text: Compare its public concern with a modern community while naming the historical differences.
Assume every city and community is identical to the original setting.
Refuse any contemporary reflection because the source is old.

questions.explanation: A careful wider-world comparison holds continuity and difference together.
